answer: A farm running 58 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the summit stake is held until the falcon settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the inlet audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 22% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one.
